evaluationLedger.note: Separate execution and exhaustive-oracle counts; excludes enumeration, hashing commitments, serialization, sorting, report and export overhead. No net-benefit claim.

decision.reason: Strictly lower registered objective than every feasible declared baseline on development and a fresh local synthetic case.

scope: Programs combine reviewed uniform-key checks, streamed partitions, conditional nested joins, and bounded hash joins.
Search is bounded enumeration of 20 programs in this declared grammar; it does not invent arbitrary operators or code.
The incumbent is the strongest feasible member of the seven declared textbook baselines on this development input.
The objective is logical operations plus the explicit auxiliary-row weight, subject to the explicit row-reference cap.

Every string comparison is charged its maximum UTF-16 input length; hash operations are charged the full key length. These are reproducible proxies; JavaScript engines can short-circuit or reuse string hashes.
Auxiliary rows count indexed and temporary partition row references, excluding shared inputs and returned output. They are not memory bytes or measured process peak memory.

Canonical output sorting, independent oracle execution, search, report generation, and export are excluded from the per-plan objective; execution and oracle search counts are reported separately in evaluationLedger.
Confirmation is a new generated public synthetic input after a local freeze, not a secret or independently administered holdout.

The duplicate-heavy example deliberately uses a different repeated key in each catalog. A known uniform-key shortcut confirms the empty join; grouping retains every missing occurrence in two proposed corrective actions.
No timing, economic return, model improvement, novel algorithm, general intelligence, or external execution claim is made.
